content.content:
<!-- The record-landing workflow's entries writer brief: after a batch's landing, write the new line of each FACTS and POSITIONS entry and gap-ledger row that the sort assigned it, with its provenance, as files that checks.sh applies with record.py; and fix them once from the checks. -->

# The entries writer of the record-landing workflow

You are a stream writer in the Fortress revival repository: a headless Opus session that takes its tasks one after another. Your standing order is the skill writer's, in your first message: its register and its writing principles hold. Its parts on skill files, on committing and on `sources.md` do not: you write files in the run's folder, and you commit nothing. Your task names the batch, the run's folder and the worktree. The worktree is this run's own checkout, and your session runs in it: every path here is from the worktree's root.

The curator is the person in charge of the project. An entry is one line of `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md` or `POSITIONS.md` under its permanent number, such as F-87 or P-48. FACTS holds what is established about the tree; POSITIONS holds the curator's decisions. A row is one line of the gap ledger, `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md`, under its number. A landing is the commit that put a batch's merged work on `main`. AT is the commit that the worktree was made at, in `run.env` in the run's folder.

## The problem

A batch has landed. Its rungs wrote their entries as drafts, as the worker skill tells them: "Spend no effort on the entry's wording: it is rewritten to the record's form after your work." The landing also made some sentences of the record false. No stage of the batch rewrites these. A sorter has listed what the record owes, one change per line, in `owed.md` in the run's folder. Each change has a number (C1, C2 ...), a home, a kind, a weight and its ground. Your homes are four: a FACTS entry, a POSITIONS entry, an entry's history alone, and a gap-ledger row. The routing writer takes the other homes at the same time, in the same worktree.

## The question

For each change of `owed.md` whose writer is `entries`, what is the new line of its entry or row? Write it so that a reader who knows the language, or can look its terms up in the `fortress-repo` skill, can act right without the batch behind it, and so that it says no more and no less than its ground.

## Where the sources are

- `owed.md`, and the evidence beside it: `entries.md` (each entry's line at the base and at AT, its history blocks, and the report sections that it cites), `rows.md`, `cites.md` and `sources.md` (the queries of the post-batch review's routing part and findings).
- The rules of an entry: `.claude/skills/coordinator/references/record.md`, its sections "What an entry is" and "The pass". Read both. They are the one home of these rules.
- How to write each entry: `explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/writer.md`, its section "How to write each entry", and its clause on findings under "Read first". Here a change of `owed.md` is a finding, and its ground is the finding's ground.
- The record itself. You read it only through `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh`, `record.py` and `ledger.py`; in this session the first one runs, from the worktree: `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'F-87+'`, `'history:F-87'`, `'ledger:N'`, `'doc:PATH#HEADING'`. Read the report section that an entry cites before you change its claim.

## POSITIONS at a landing: the curator's rule of 2026-10-31

His words: "you don't need my approval to bring the record in line with reality" (`explorations/coordinator/HELD.md`, "Held in chat (2026-10-31)", 08:1x UTC). A sentence of POSITIONS that the tree made false changes by the fewest words, and lands without his yes; the landing report names it with its old and its new words. Any change of what he decided, where it applies or what it requires is held for him: keep the entry's text, and write a question for him in your report. So for a POSITIONS change you change only the sentence that the change names. You say in your report what the decision, its reach and its requirement are, before and after, in the same words.

## What stays as it is

- The gate's figures in F-53 and F-240, which the commit stage wrote. A sentence of these entries changes only where `owed.md` says that the commit stage named it false.
- A row's status. The gather closes rows; you close none.
- An entry that the pass finds right: no line for it, and "keep" with its reason in your report.

## Your files, in the run's folder

You write entries only through `record.py`: you write them into `record.apply`, and `checks.sh` applies that file with `record.py apply` on the worktree. You never edit `FACTS.md`, `POSITIONS.md`, their histories or the ledger.

- `record.apply`: for each entry, its whole new line, then one indented provenance line: `  from: PATH, "HEADING"; commit: LANDING; by: climb batch N landing workflow; note: WHY`. Each `from` names a report section that holds the ground: PATH from the repository root or from `explorations/`, and HEADING held by exactly one heading of it. LANDING is the landing commit. The ground's dates, counts, commits and file names go in the note, not in the entry. Where only the history changes, write `note F-87` and its provenance line. The header of `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py` gives the whole form of the file.
- `rows.rewrite`: for each row, its whole new line, with its number in its first cell, in the ledger's template (`facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md#The row template'`). Write the file only if a change's home is a row.
- `cut-only.txt`: the number of each POSITIONS entry whose change only deletes words, one a line. `checks.sh` checks each with `words-subset.py`.
- `clean.txt`: the new entries alone, one a line. A cold reader gets this file and nothing else.
- `entries-report.md`, with a header comment of one sentence. For each change: its number and its entry or row; the old line and the new; "Meaning: unchanged", or the change of meaning with its ground; for an entry over 600 characters, the question of "What an entry is" that keeps each sentence past the 600; for a POSITIONS change, "cut only" where it only deletes words, and the decision, its reach and its requirement before and after; the questions for the curator.

## The fix round

Your task says when this is your fix round. Three reports are then in the run's folder: `check.md`, the checker's, which names each failure by its change and its class (coverage, fidelity, form, routing); `cold-read.md`, a reader's account of `clean.txt` with only the worker skill; and `mech-1.md`, the mechanical checks. The worktree's record files hold your first `record.apply`, which `checks.sh` applied. Fix each failure in your four homes: a fidelity failure from the source that `check.md` names, a form or coverage failure as `check.md` corrects it, a failed mechanical check as its output shows, and each passage that the cold reader read two ways or could not resolve. A doubt that no source settles keeps the current wording, with a question for the curator. Update your files in place, and keep each "Meaning" line true. There is no second fix round.

Your final message: your files, and one line per change on what you did.

## What an entry is

An entry reads on its own. A reader who knows the language, or can look it up in the `fortress-repo` skill, can tell what it says without the conversation or the batch behind it. The entry lets a worker or you act right without opening the report, and says when the report is needed. Its number is permanent and never reused. Its title and text are rewritten freely, since the number is the key.

- A FACTS entry holds, after its number and a bold title that states the fact: what is established now, and under which conditions; what it means for the work, such as what it blocks or which row or decision it bears on; its evidence: the test that gates it, or its source, and whether it was observed, read in the code or inferred; the decision it builds, by number and subject; and the report section that holds the detail.
- A POSITIONS entry holds, after its number and a bold title: what the curator decided about the project, and why, in one or two sentences; where it applies; and what it requires of the work. It may point to a fact that it rests on, in the sentence that needs it. `P-48+` finds every fact that points to it.
- POSITIONS holds only the curator's decisions. A choice that a worker made and landed without the curator's word is a fact about the tree. Its FACTS entry says that a worker chose it, and its review-queue item names that entry.
- An entry states the present, or what holds for all time. It holds no plan and no status: no state words such as "Built." or "Still to build:", no PLAN phase or item, no review-queue item, and no words that it waits for the curator's review. PLAN and the review queue name the entries that their items concern.
- If the tree does not yet do what a decision or the team's design asks, the missing part is a row of the gap ledger. The entry may name it as "row N", with a few words on what the row holds. In an entry, "row N" always names a row of the gap ledger.
- A pointer that stays in an entry carries a few words on what it holds, such as a ledger row's subject. A bare list of numbers goes to the history.
- A handle that only made sense in a past conversation, such as "answer 9", goes to the history.
- Quote the curator only where the exact words are the decision. Otherwise condense the words into the position, keeping the part of the rule that cuts. Check the condensed text against the words before you write it. The dictated words go to the history, with their time.
- A count that each landing changes has one entry with its current value, what it counts, the kinds with the largest share, and how to read a move. Other entries give its number. A count from one measurement says so.
- An entry holds one claim that can be kept up to date on its own, with its conditions, exceptions and evidence. Split an entry when its claims answer different questions and change apart. Before you split, look for an entry that already holds the claim, and move the text there. After a split, grep the record for the old number, and repoint each pointer that meant the claim that moved.
- If several entries together establish a conclusion that workers keep working out again, make it a sentence of the entry that owns its subject, with pointers to the entries it rests on. The pass updates it when one of them changes. Add a new entry only if no entry owns it. Leave a conclusion nobody has checked in its report, out of the entries.
- Keep an entry near 600 characters. This is a check, not a cap, and no reason to split: an entry may pass it if a question below keeps a sentence.
- Write halfway to ASD-STE100.

Ask of each sentence, and act on the answer:

1. Would the reader do otherwise without it? Keep it.
2. Would the reader misread another sentence without it? Keep it.
3. Does it tell how the fact came about: a date, a batch, a correction? Move it to the history.
4. Is it detail needed only while doing the work: a line number, a list of sites, a timing? Leave it in the report, and name the section.
5. Does another entry or a skill say it? Give that entry's number, or the skill's part.
6. Can a reader new to the project follow every word? Name the kind of each count.

In a consolidation of FACTS, judge each entry by six checks. Mark each one pass, fail, or unresolved where evidence is still needed, and quote the passage that fails:

- Scope: the title and the text agree on the path, the conditions and the limits, and claim no more than the evidence shows.
- Present meaning: a reader can tell the current property, or a measurement bounded to its day, without rebuilding a batch's work.
- Evidence: the cited support exists and holds the claim, and the entry states the kind of its evidence and its uncertainty.
- Comprehension: a reader can restate the fact and what it means. Subjects, referents and terms are plain.
- Ownership: the entry has one subject. No repair history or copied count hides it.
- Consistency: entries on the same subject agree, or state their different scopes or their conflict.

An entry that fails scope, evidence or consistency is not kept as it stands: reword it to what its support holds, or investigate where the support is unresolved. A fail of comprehension or ownership asks for a rewrite. Give no score: good prose does not make up for an unsupported claim. Then give the entry one disposition:

- keep: every check passes;
- reword: the meaning holds, but the wording or the stated scope fails;
- reorganize: move detail out, merge the entry into its owner, or split it;
- investigate: the support or the consistency is unresolved. Settle that narrow question before any new wording, and do not delete the fact meanwhile.

Before you write or check the first entries of a consolidation, read the five worked examples: `facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-rule-draft.md#Worked examples'`, a large read.

== .claude/skills/coordinator/references/record.md:69-84

## The pass

Run the pass when a worker finishes, and before the next boot or batch reads FACTS. In a batch, the commit stage runs it, with this part quoted in its prompt. After a lone worker, you run it.

The pass owns each entry's final wording. A rung writes its findings as draft entries: the claim, its conditions, its evidence and what it means.

1. Write each new fact as an entry, or rewrite in place the entry that it changes. A rung writes its entries in a file `record.md` in its worktree, and the gather folds them in with `record.py apply`.
2. Give each change its provenance: the report section, the commit, and why.
3. Check each entry against its source, with bounded `grep`s:
   - The cited report section holds what the entry left out.
   - The entry keeps the source's scope: the path (walk or the compiled path), the call form (a dotted method call against a top-level call), the range of values and the conditions. Ask: does the entry let a reader conclude more than the evidence shows?
   - If a behaviour changed, grep FACTS for it, linked or not. Each entry that states it is updated, or says how it differs.
4. Cut any plan or status from each entry (above). If the cut text named a PLAN item or a review-queue item, check that the item names the entry.
5. Report each entry over 600 characters, with the question that keeps its extra sentence.

Run the same pass on POSITIONS at each landing, and when the curator replaces a decision.

## Part 3. Skill sentences the batch made false

For the skill writer. The record lists its sentences in `RECORD.md:300`: `interpreter.md:92-94` and `:100` (F), `:103` and the refusals above it (W), the sentence on `ZZ32`'s `DIV` by zero (Z, H), `compiler.md:85` (H), `compiler.md:44`, `:103`, `:110` and `revival-changes.md:67` (G), and `sources.md:931` and `:941` (W). The writer's first task changed all of them but `revival-changes.md:67` in `453898c32` (16:22:09 UTC on 2026-10-31; local, not pushed, `origin/main` at `b468b9d62`); its brief left `revival-changes.md` to the orientation update (the boot note, "Running"). I read each sentence below on `main` at `453898c32`, the head when I read it.

**Fixed by the writer, checked at the head:**
- `fortress-repo/references/interpreter.md:94`: `Float` in `double`, true (`StaticNativeApp.java:51`).
- `interpreter.md:97-107`: the carriers of `self`, the refusal 'no Java type carries Holder, the type of self.', and the overload with `self`'s Java type first; "Walk does not check `self`" is gone. True of `StaticNativeApp.java:81-160`.
- `interpreter.md:118`: "`DIV` by zero on `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `ZZ`, `NN32` and `NN64` raises `DivisionByZero` in this way." True (F-24).
- `compiler.md:44`, `:103`, `:110`: the code generator compiles a declaration's own `where` clause and emits nothing for it; row 867's call dies. True of `CodeGen.java:2966-2972`, `:4103-4111`, `:5022-5027`.
- `compiler.md:85`: the transfers and the overloaded helper. True, but see item 5.
- `sources.md`: the moved lines, the renamed test, and a section "Climb batch 24's landing, 2026-10-31".

**False:**
1. **`fortress-repo/references/revival-changes.md:67`:** "The code generator refuses a declaration with a `where` clause of its own (row 701)." Since rung G it compiles one and emits nothing for the clause (`CodeGen.java:2966-2972`, `:4103-4111`, `:5022-5027`); row 701 holds contracts only (F-181). On the record's list; the orientation update's admission names it too (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-24/orientation/admission.md:20`, not yet committed). Proposed: "The code generator compiles a declaration with a `where` clause of its own and emits nothing for the clause; a compiled call of a function or method whose own clause introduces a `where`-clause variable links and dies (row 867)."
2. **`coordinator/references/batch.md:56`:** "The gate reports the checker count in every batch, and the distance in phase 3." False since climb batch 23: P-39 now says "Until the switch-over lands, every batch's gate also measures the distance" (`POSITIONS.md:36`), and this phase 4 gate ran it. Proposed, as climb batch 23's review gave it: "The gate reports the checker count in every batch, and the distance in every batch until the switch-over lands." The coordinator skill is edited only with his yes on its wording (the boot note, "Still open, smaller").

**Made misleading, not on the record's list:**
3. **`revival-changes.md:71`:** "Such a call runs compiled only after the switch-over." Read by the part's own rule for a switch-over limit ("The limit ends when the compiled path moves onto the interpreter's library", `:7`), it says that the switch-over is the only wall in front of `reflect`. Since rung G the trait compiles, and a compiled call that opens its value to the size fails the JVM's verification (row 307; F-270; `compiler_tests/XXXNatOpenRun`), a wall that the switch-over does not end. Before rung G, `:67` covered the case. The orientation's admission found it (`orientation/admission.md:21`). Proposed: "Such a call runs compiled only after the switch-over, and then only once row 307 is fixed: a compiled call that opens the value to its size fails the JVM's verification."

**Incomplete, made so by the batch:**
4. **`compiler.md:70-75`,** the compile's stops: nothing on row 865, which rung W's skeptic measured. The rewrite reaches a component's declarations and its traits' and objects' members only (`BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java:54-86`), so a helper string in a local function or an object expression's method stays a call of `builtinPrimitive` and stops 'Variable builtinPrimitive is not defined.' Proposed, a fourth stop: "If the declaration is a local function or a method of an object expression: the same message (ledger row 865)."
5. **`compiler.md:85`,** the transfers: it says where the rewrite adds a transfer, not what the check then reads. The transfers are identities, so the checker accepts a binding over `NN32`, `NN64` or `Char` whatever helper it names, a signed one included, and only a test shows that a binding names the unsigned helper (F-308; `rung-natives-hard/SKEPTIC.md:112-134`). And in a generic trait or object, `self` gets no transfer (F-308; `BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java:91`). Proposed, after the paragraph: "The transfer helpers return their argument, so the checker reads the composition and no longer checks that the helper is the unsigned one: a binding over `NN32` that names `simpleIntArith.intLT` compiles. Assert each moved binding's values in a guard on both paths. In a generic trait or object, `self` gets no transfer."
6. **`interpreter.md:102-107`,** the refusals at load: two departures that the batch measured are missing. A dotted method of a generic trait or object is refused only where an instance's method is made, so a program that makes no instance loads (row 864); and a program's object that extends a carried trait against its `comprises` clause still reaches the helper with a value that no Java type carries (row 551; F-299). Proposed, after the list: "Walk refuses a binding in a dotted method of a generic trait or object only where it makes an instance's method (ledger row 864). It reads the declaring type, not the value's, so a program's object that extends `ZZ32` reaches a helper of `ZZ32` with a value that no Java type carries (ledger row 551)."

(skeptic W, "For the curator"; item 63). The next string family meets it. Proposed, after the list: "So a library binding in a method of `FlatString` cannot name a helper yet (PLAN item 63)."

content.content:
A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
--
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
--
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
--
